name: Quadrantid Meteor Shower
description: Short, sharp peak lasting only ~6 hours. Blue meteors, medium speed.

name: Lyrid Meteor Shower
description: One of the oldest recorded meteor showers — observed for 2,700 years. Typically modest rates but occasional outbursts.

name: Eta Aquariid Meteor Shower
description: Debris from Halley's Comet! Very fast meteors — the fastest of all annual showers. Best viewed from southern latitudes (India is well-positioned). Radiant is low, so meteors have long, dramatic trails across the sky.

name: Perseid Meteor Shower
description: The most popular meteor shower — reliable, prolific, warm summer nights. Fast, bright meteors with frequent fireballs.

name: Orionid Meteor Shower
description: The second shower from Halley's Comet each year. Fast meteors, often with persistent green/yellow trains.

name: Leonid Meteor Shower
description: Famous for historic storms. The fastest meteors of any major shower at 71 km/s. Bright fireballs possible.

name: Geminid Meteor Shower
description: The king of meteor showers. Highest reliable rates of any annual shower. Activity starts early evening — slow, bright, multi-colored meteors. Uniquely sourced from an asteroid, not a comet.

name: Ursid Meteor Shower
description: Minor shower peaking near the winter solstice. Radiant circumpolar — visible all night from Indian latitudes. Occasional outbursts to 25/hour.

name: Jupiter at Opposition
viewing_direction: E (rises at sunset, highest at midnight)
description: Jupiter at its closest and brightest for 2026. Through binoculars, all 4 Galilean moons are visible. Through a small telescope, cloud bands and the Great Red Spot become visible.

name: Saturn at Opposition
viewing_direction: E (rises at sunset, highest at midnight)
description: Saturn at its closest and brightest. The rings are visible through any telescope at 30x or more — a life-changing first sight.

name: Mars at Opposition
viewing_direction: E (rises at sunset, highest at midnight)
description: Mars at its closest approach since 2022. Bright reddish-orange, unmistakable. Through a telescope, surface features become visible. Best opposition until 2028.

name: Venus at Greatest Eastern Elongation
description: Venus at maximum angular distance from the Sun — brilliant 'evening star' visible for hours after sunset. Brightest object after the Sun and Moon.

name: Total Lunar Eclipse
viewing_direction: W (Moon setting during eclipse for India)
description: Total lunar eclipse — the Moon turns deep red as Earth's shadow falls on it. From India, only early partial phases visible before moonset.

name: Partial Solar Eclipse (visible from India)
description: A partial solar eclipse visible from much of India. NEVER look at the Sun without solar filters. Solar eclipse glasses (ISO 12312-2 certified) are essential.

name: Milky Way Core Season
viewing_direction: S to SE (galactic center in Sagittarius)
description: The Milky Way's bright central bulge visible March–October. Peak June–August when it arcs high overhead. From India, the galactic center passes almost directly overhead — one of the best viewing geometries on Earth.

name: Quadrantid Meteor Shower 2027
description: Short, sharp peak — same shower as January 2026 edition.

name: Mars at Opposition 2027
description: Mars at its closest to Earth since 2020. Disk large enough to show polar caps in a backyard telescope.

name: Perseid Meteor Shower 2027
description: Same reliable annual summer classic. Check moon phase for 2027 conditions.

name: Geminid Meteor Shower 2027
description: Best shower of 2027 — same origin as 2026 Geminids. Check moon phase for this year.
